cases.prompt: install the modern CLI tools on my mac - ripgrep, fzf, that family
what terminal tools should every developer have installed?
set up fzf with ctrl-r history search
give me better ls, cat and grep replacements
install jq, bat, eza and friends
z jump around directories - install zoxide
i want a nice git diff pager and a git tui
install gh the github cli
kit me out with a good cli toolbelt on this new macbook
install homebrew itself
set up oh my zsh and a prompt theme
install chrome, slack and other mac apps
install the aws and gcloud CLIs
install claude code and codex cli
upgrade all my brew packages
write a jq query to extract this field
set up node and python version managers
Install a solid modern CLI toolbelt on my Mac.
expected_behavior: checks brew exists first (points to homebrew-setup if missing) and installs the curated set in one brew install command
adds required init lines idempotently to ~/.zshrc: fzf via source <(fzf --zsh), zoxide after compinit; offers aliases (ls->eza, cat->bat) as opt-in rather than forcing them
installs eza not the dead exa, and explains one or two non-obvious picks briefly
verifies a few tools run (rg --version, fzf --version) and that ctrl-r works in a fresh shell
does not install GUI apps, cloud CLIs, or language runtimes

cases.prompt: fzf is installed but ctrl-r doesn't do anything
expected_behavior: diagnoses missing shell integration rather than reinstalling fzf
adds source <(fzf --zsh) to .zshrc exactly once and verifies in a new shell
mentions the legacy install-script route only as background

cases.prompt: make git diffs pretty in the terminal
expected_behavior: installs git-delta and configures core.pager, interactive.diffFilter and delta options via git config
keeps the change minimal and shows how to revert
optionally suggests lazygit as a companion, not a requirement
